title: 2026-06-25 Hosted API demo: chat/text generation basics — LumenPay
summary: Intro demo of Redwood Hosted API for chat/text generation. Covered streaming, request parameters, retry semantics, SDK examples, Console monitoring, and Optimize recommendations. Discussed security (SOC2, KMS), latency vs cost tradeoffs, and next steps for a small pilot and security follow-up.
action_items: Alex Kim | Send tailored pricing and rate card + pilot proposal | 2026-06-28
Jordan Lee | Share simple benchmark script and instructions for a 1k request test | 2026-06-29
Alex Kim | Provide SOC 2 and security whitepaper links | 2026-06-26
next_steps: Customer to confirm pilot scope (expected 2-week pilot) and target endpoints
Redwood to send pricing and security docs
Schedule technical POC kickoff with LumenPay SREs next Tuesday (proposed 2026-07-01)
Customer to run benchmark script and share results
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I see Maria, Ethan, Sana — thanks. We'll run through the Hosted API demo, focus on chat/text generation basics, streaming, core params and retries, and then show a quick Console view and Optimize tips.

[00:18] Maria Gonzales: Great, thanks. Quick context — we're building an in-app assistant for payments flow, needs short latency, and strict PII controls. We're evaluating hosted first.

[00:32] Jordan Lee: Awesome. We'll highlight latency and data controls — hosted can often hit your SLOs but we'll talk dedicated/private later if needed. Quick question — what's your throughput and typical request size?

[00:45] Ethan Park: On average 50 requests per second during peak, most requests are 120-300 tokens, occasional long threads to 2k tokens.

[00:57] Jordan Lee: That's really helpful. Hosted API can handle that with proper batching and streaming. We'll show streaming for low tail latency. Also note caching — prefix/KV cache helps with repeated prompts.

[01:15] Sana Arora: Any concerns about data residency and encryption at rest? We need KMS and audit logs.

[01:22] Alex Kim: Yes, Redwood Hosted offers customer-managed keys integrations and audit logs; I'll share the security whitepaper after. We'll also cover retry semantics so you can keep idempotency.

[01:35] Jordan Lee: Jumping into the demo — I'm going to open a quick notebook and a curl example. First, streaming. When you stream tokens, the server flushes partial tokens so UI can render sooner. This is a typical pattern for chat.

[01:50] [Screen-share starts]

[02:00] Jordan Lee: Here's a python snippet using our SDK; notice the stream=True flag. We also show a low-level streaming SSE example. The important part is how to handle partial events and finalization.

[02:18] Maria Gonzales: Is there jitter on the SSE stream during bursts?

[02:22] Jordan Lee: There can be perceived jitter if you're not buffering client-side; we recommend an 80-120ms aggregator window for UI. Also server-side we respect small token flushes to keep latency low.

[02:40] Ethan Park: What about retries — if we get a 5xx mid-stream, how do we resume?

[02:45] Alex Kim: Good question. For idempotent calls, we recommend a request_id header on each request. For streaming specifically, if mid-stream fails, best practice is to retry the whole request and present a fallback in UI. We also provide automatic retry hooks in the SDK with exponential backoff, and a final guarantee to avoid duplicate side effects if you pass idempotency keys.

[03:10] Jordan Lee: Also worth noting: our server returns structured error codes for transient vs permanent errors. You can wire different UI behavior.

[03:22] [Timestamps every ~30s moving through demo]

[03:28] Jordan Lee: Now parameters. Temperature controls randomness, top_p is nucleus sampling. We walked through extremes — temp 0.0 for deterministic, 0.8 for creative. Max_tokens caps output length. Stop sequences are supported.

[03:44] Maria Gonzales: For our compliance flows we need deterministic outputs for certain prompts. So we'd set temp to 0?

[03:49] Jordan Lee: Yep, temp=0 is common. Also you can pin model version and use Redwood Optimize suggestions to pick quantization profiles that avoid hallucinations for your dataset.

[04:05] Ethan Park: The Optimize product — can it recommend batching and quantization automatically per route?

[04:10] Alex Kim: Yes, Optimize analyzes token distributions and traffic patterns, then recommends batching window sizes, cache keys, and quantization settings. It's surfaced in the Console with expected cost impact estimates. We'll show a sample Optimize dashboard.

[04:28] [Screen shows Console]

[04:33] Jordan Lee: Here is the per-route dashboard — latency P50/P95, cost per 1k tokens, token breakdown, and a visual for batch sizes. You can set autoscale policies and canary rollouts from the same UI.

[04:50] Sana Arora: Do we get token-level traces tied to request IDs? We need that for debugging.

[04:56] Jordan Lee: Yes, request IDs are carried through and you can click into a trace, see per-token timing, and correlate to infra nodes. There's also a retention policy for logs (configurable).

[05:12] Maria Gonzales: About encryption — you mentioned KMS. Is it customer-managed?

[05:16] Alex Kim: For Hosted, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), and we have options for Bring Your Own Key (BYOK). We'll attach the security doc.

[05:28] Ethan Park: Any SOC/ISO compliance?

[05:31] Alex Kim: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we also provide ISO docs on request. I'll attach those.

[05:38] Jordan Lee: Back to the code — here's a curl example showing retries: we include Idempotency-Key and use a 429/5xx retry policy with jittered exponential backoff.

[05:52] Maria Gonzales: How do you recommend handling token limits for multi-turn chat threads?

[05:58] Jordan Lee: You can either compress context (summarize previous turns) or use our KV cache to store embeddings or prefix tokens — K V cache will give you partial reuse and reduce tokens per request. For very long threads we recommend summarization or context-window management.

[06:18] Ethan Park: For LumenPay payments assistant, we also plan to call internal verification microservices — any suggested patterns to avoid leaking data to models?

[06:27] Alex Kim: Keep PII out of prompts where possible. If you must include, use redaction at edge or tokenization and use private deployments for sensitive workloads. For hosted, you can opt out of data retention and enable encryption/MFA.

[06:42] Maria Gonzales: Can Redwood hosted support VPC peering or private endpoints?

[06:47] Jordan Lee: Yes, we offer VPC endpoints for hosted customers and Private deployment for stricter isolation — we can discuss Dedicated capacity if you need guaranteed throughput/latency SLAs.

[07:00] [Minor audio overlap, speaker label shows as Speaker 1 for a line]

[07:10] Jordan Lee: Moving on, monitoring. The Console also surfaces failed-call reasons and automatic alerts. You can tie alerts to Slack/PagerDuty.

[07:22] Sana Arora: For the pilot, what's the typical onboarding time?

[07:27] Alex Kim: For a small pilot, you can be live within a week — usually a couple of integration days and a quick validation run. For Dedicated or Private it takes longer (multi-week).

[07:38] Jordan Lee: I'm going to run a small live sample: send prompt -> stream partial tokens -> complete.

[07:45] [Live sample run: small delay while demo executes]

[08:02] Jordan Lee: You can see the partial tokens come in at ~80ms intervals then finalization. This gives sub-200ms perceived latency for short outputs.

[08:20] Ethan Park: What's the per-token cost ballpark?

[08:24] Alex Kim: Depends on model — we'll send rate cards. Optimize can estimate cost savings for batching and cache. For typical chat configs we show examples in the pricing deck.

[08:36] Maria Gonzales: Any known differences against OpenAI w.r.t streaming?

[08:40] Jordan Lee: Similar in concept, but Redwood focuses on production features: per-route cost breakdown, built-in autoscaling controls, and Optimize recommendations. Also our fallback routing can move requests between model variants for graceful degradation.

[09:00] [Mid-demo Q&A — paraphrased and natural hesitation]

[09:10] Maria Gonzales: Quick nit — do you have sample rate-limiting headers so we can surface to users?

[09:15] Jordan Lee: Yes, the response includes x-rate-limit remaining and reset. We emit headers and webhook-based quota alerts.

[09:27] Ethan Park: For retries and idempotency, do SDKs persist keys locally? We want to avoid reuse across devices.

[09:33] Alex Kim: We recommend generating a per-request idempotency key server-side — that way mobile clients don't create collisions. SDKs give you a helper to generate UUID keys.

[09:45] [Timestamps jump as demo wraps into Console features]

[10:02] Jordan Lee: I'll show a short Optimize example — here's a recommended batching window for your token distribution. It projects a 30% cost drop with a 5% latency increase at P95; you can tune the policy.

[10:20] Maria Gonzales: Good to know. For the pilot, we'd like Redwood to recommend a conservative config that prioritizes latency.

[10:27] Alex Kim: Noted — we'll propose a low-latency pilot config.

[10:33] Sana Arora: Any logging concerns for PCI data?

[10:38] Jordan Lee: We do not recommend sending raw card data to models; use tokenization or send references. For PCI scope, a private/on-prem deployment is the safest route.

[10:50] [Wrap-up portion — 10-20 mins of action recaps and questions]

[11:02] Alex Kim: Recap: we'll send pricing, SOC2/security docs, the benchmark script, and a pilot proposal with low-latency defaults. Customer will decide pilot scope and run the benchmark.

[11:15] Maria Gonzales: Sounds good. Can you also include a short guide for streaming implementation on our React front-end?

[11:21] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll include a front-end snippet and recommended buffering strategy.

[11:28] Ethan Park: If pilot looks good, timeline to migrate some traffic to Redwood? We're thinking gradual rollouts over 6-8 weeks.

[11:36] Alex Kim: That's typical — can do canary routing via the Console and A/B test.

[11:43] Maria Gonzales: Ok, let's target the 2-week pilot starting 2026-07-06 if we can finalize details.

[11:51] Alex Kim: We'll aim to get docs and pricing to you by Friday and propose the POC kickoff for 2026-07-01.

[12:00] [Meeting ends; brief small talk]

Notes: occasional transcription errors — 'K V cache' spelled out, 'samel' heard for SAML in one line, speaker attribution had one line labeled Speaker 1 during audio overlap. Shared artifacts: pricing deck (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/pricing-lumenpay), security whitepaper (link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-whitepaper), benchmark script (link: https://redwood.ai/samples/benchmark-lumenpay).
